sections.html:
East Chicago is a Lake County city on the shore of Lake Michigan, about 18 miles from downtown Chicago and just west of Gary. It covers about 14.9 square miles, including roughly 0.7 square miles of water.

Three waterways define the map: Lake Michigan, the Grand Calumet River and the Indiana Harbor and Ship Canal. The land started as swamp, and the city took its name from its position east of Chicago.

FactEast Chicago
Total area14.86 square miles
Elevation587 feet
2020 census population26,370
2010 census population29,698
Peak population57,669 (1960)
Population estimate, July 202525,610

The city has lost people for decades, and the Census Bureau estimate shows a further 2.9% drop between April 2020 and July 2025.

sections.h2: How did steel shape East Chicago?
sections.html:
Steel made East Chicago. The town incorporated in 1889 and became a city in 1893. Its population was 1,255 in 1890 and 3,411 by 1900.

Inland Steel arrived in 1903, and the Indiana Harbor Ship Canal gave the mills a navigable link to Lake Michigan by 1907. Inland's capacity grew from 60,000 tons in 1903 to a peak of 8.6 million tons in 1978. During World War I the city was nicknamed the Arsenal of America.

The steel crisis of 1974 to 1986 cut into jobs, and ownership of the mills changed several times: Ispat International bought Inland Steel in 1998, the mills were merged into ArcelorMittal in 2004, and Cleveland-Cliffs bought them in 2020. Cleveland-Cliffs' Indiana Harbor Works is described as the largest steel mill in the United States.

  • Other employers named for the city: U.S. Steel's East Chicago Tin, Union Tank Car, American Steel Foundries, USG and St. Catherine Hospital.
  • A casino opened in 1997 as the Showboat Casino with about 900 employees.

Indiana Harbor was where most of the mill's working families lived, which explains why the city's older housing sits close to the industrial lakefront.

sections.h2: What are the neighborhoods of East Chicago?
sections.html:
East Chicago has long been described as a twin city. Indiana Harbor, the East Side, grew around Inland Steel and housed most working families, while the West Side was the residential area of the native-born business community.

Two sites in the city are on the National Register of Historic Places: the Marktown Historic District and the Indiana Harbor Public Library. A house in Marktown may be subject to rules for historic properties, which a buyer will ask about.

The city also contains the West Calumet public housing area and the neighborhoods around it, which come up again in the lead section below.

sections.h2: What do the census numbers say about East Chicago housing?
sections.html:
East Chicago has more renters than owners. The Census Bureau reports 42.9% owner-occupied housing for 2020 to 2024, a median owner-occupied value of $105,400 and median gross rent of $854.

The 2020 census counted 11,735 housing units, and 16.0% of them were vacant. Owners of a house that has sat empty or needs work should expect a buyer to ask for an inspection and possibly price in repairs.

sections.h2: What is the USS Lead Superfund site in East Chicago?
sections.html:
The USS Lead Superfund site is a residential area north of a former lead smelter where soil was contaminated with lead. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency says the smelter operated from about 1906 to 1985, and the site includes about 1,200 homes, parks, schools and public buildings.

On October 2, 2020, EPA removed 671 cleaned-up properties from the Superfund National Priorities List. The agency stated that lead-contaminated soil had been removed from 95% of the 1,078 mostly residential properties in Zones 2 and 3, and that the 671 properties were cleared for residential use. Properties not yet finished stayed on the list, and all Zone 1 properties remained on it until remediated.

  • Cleanup target for soil: 400 mg/kg of lead.
  • Properties removed from the list may be eligible for the city's Residential Repair Program.
  • EPA continues to look at possible groundwater issues in the area.

These are archived EPA statements, so check the agency's current pages for the status of a specific address. If your house is in or near the site, expect buyers and their lenders to ask about it.

sections.h2: Which schools and transit serve East Chicago?
sections.html:
The School City of East Chicago serves the whole city, and all residents are zoned to Central High School. Charter options include East Chicago Urban Enterprise for kindergarten through eighth grade and East Chicago Lighthouse Charter School. Ivy Tech Community College has a presence in the city.

A South Shore Line station is in East Chicago, and East Chicago Transit runs free buses on three routes: Crosstown, West Calumet and Griffith Plaza. Indiana State Road 912, the Cline Avenue Expressway, links the city to the Indiana Toll Road and the Borman Expressway.

  • U.S. 12 runs through Indiana Harbor and U.S. 20 runs through East Chicago.
  • Nearest Amtrak: the Wolverine at the Hammond-Whiting station, about 5.5 miles away.
  • Chicago Midway is the nearest airport with scheduled service.

sections.h2: What must a landlord do when selling or holding rental property in East Chicago?
sections.html:
East Chicago requires owners of rental housing to register each property every year by January 31. The registration form comes from the City Controller's office, and the city will not accept it without proof of insurance equal to the property value or a bond or letter of credit.

A new owner must register within 30 days of obtaining title. A late fee applies to each unit not registered by April 15 each year, and failing to register is a violation with a fine per unit. Each day of violation counts as a separate offense. The city sets the dollar amounts, which the code section does not list.

A landlord selling a tenant-occupied house should confirm the registration is current, because a buyer will want a clean record. Only 42.9% of occupied homes in the city are owner-occupied, so rental sales are a regular part of the local market.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded and property taxes paid for an East Chicago house?
sections.html:
East Chicago is in Lake County, so deeds are recorded with the Lake County Recorder at 2293 N. Main Street, Building A, second floor, Crown Point. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, at 219-755-3730.

Property tax goes to the Lake County Treasurer, 219-755-3760. Indiana's two installments for 2026 were due May 11 and November 10, with a 5% penalty for payments up to 30 days late and 10% beyond that.

Lake County's delinquent list is compiled by July 1 or 51 days after the due date, and the tax sale is held online. If you are behind and want to sell, ask the title company to pay the balance from your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Is it hard to sell a house in the USS Lead area of East Chicago?
faqs.a: It can take longer, since buyers and lenders ask whether the property was cleaned up. EPA says 671 properties were removed from the Superfund list on October 2, 2020, and that they were cleared for residential use. Properties not yet finished stayed on the list.

faqs.q: When must East Chicago landlords register rental property?
faqs.a: By January 31 each year, with proof of insurance or a bond. New owners must register within 30 days of obtaining title, and a late fee applies to units not registered by April 15.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in East Chicago?
faqs.a: At the Lake County Recorder's office in Crown Point, 2293 N. Main Street, Building A, second floor. Call 219-755-3730 for hours and requirements.

faqs.q: How much is a typical home worth in East Chicago?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied value of $105,400 for 2020 to 2024. Your own house may sit well above or below that depending on condition.

faqs.q: What school district is East Chicago in?
faqs.a: The School City of East Chicago serves the whole city, and residents are zoned to Central High School. Two charter schools also operate in the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell my East Chicago house if it is vacant or needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Vacant and damaged houses are common here, with 16.0% of housing units vacant at the 2020 census. A direct buyer who purchases as-is avoids the repair requests that often follow a lender appraisal.
